answer: An agent economy can resist sybils through bonded identity graphs: each agent is a vertex on the settlement graph that must lock an escalating bond, guaranteed by one real-world bridge of attestations, so fabricating identities grows expensive instead of free. Around each vertex a vine of historical peer ratings winds over time, giving a bond full weight only after consistent behavior across several epochs, which makes mass-produced puppets unprofitable long before they could earn real trust.
